title: Your First Financial Year

conceptsAssessed.concept: Cover needs, allow reasonable wants, and allocate limited income.
Build and protect accessible emergency savings.
Judge borrowing by purpose, affordability, and repayment pressure.
Recognise pressure, secrecy, guarantees, and unsafe requests.
Create a measurable and affordable financial goal.
Invest only when ready, diversify, and respond thoughtfully to volatility.

learningObjective: Apply budgeting, saving, emergency planning, debt management, scam awareness, goal-setting, and investing concepts across one simulated financial year.
primaryMisconception: Long-term wealth comes mainly from one lucky investment rather than a series of consistent financial decisions.
secondaryMisconceptions: Investing should always come before building emergency savings.
One financial mistake permanently ruins a person’s financial future.
A higher investment balance automatically means stronger financial health.
keyTakeaway: Financial strength comes from consistent decisions, not one lucky investment.

overview.summary: Manage twelve months of salary, essentials, enjoyment, savings, an emergency, debt, a scam, a measurable goal, investment readiness, and a market decline. Earlier decisions change later options. The final dashboard rewards stability, protection, evidence-based decisions, and adaptability rather than the luckiest investment result.

screens.title: Your First Financial Year
screens.content: Twelve salaries. One major goal. A repair, a scam, and a market drop are coming. Can your plan stay balanced?
screens.illustration: A twelve-month calendar with salary, bills, savings, scam, goal, and investment icons.

screens.title: A New Monthly Income
screens.content: Your first full-time job pays Rs. 100,000 monthly. You begin with Rs. 20,000 savings and no debt.
screens.illustration: Salary, savings, emergency, debt, and goal cards.

screens.title: Several Jobs for One Salary
screens.content: Your income must cover essentials, enjoyment, emergency protection, and a Rs. 180,000 professional goal.
screens.illustration: Four containers labelled needs, wants, emergency, and goal.

screens.title: Choices Carry Forward
screens.content: Money saved early creates options later. Debt, scam losses, and missed bills reduce future flexibility.
screens.illustration: A timeline linking early decisions to later events.

screens.title: What Builds the Strongest Year?
screens.question: Which approach is most likely to create a stable financial year?

options.label: Invest every spare rupee

options.label: Balance needs, enjoyment, savings, goals, and protection

stages.title: Your First Salary
stages.situation: Your first Rs. 100,000 salary arrives. Classify expenses and build a monthly plan that covers essentials while leaving room for protection, goals, and reasonable enjoyment.
stages.objective: Classify ten expenses and create a valid monthly budget.

config.ambiguityExplanation: Mobile access may be essential for work. Restaurant food may be optional or practical when no alternative exists.

choices.label: Balanced valid budget
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Selected allocations become the monthly plan.
choices.shortTermConsequence: Needs and future priorities receive clear limits.
choices.laterConsequence: Later emergency and goal options use these allocations.
choices.immediateFeedback: The budget protects current needs while creating future options.
choices.classificationReason: Essentials, saving, protection, and affordable enjoyment all fit.

choices.label: Valid budget with no entertainment
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Optional enjoyment is redirected to saving or cash.
choices.laterConsequence: The plan may be harder to maintain.
choices.immediateFeedback: A no-entertainment plan can work temporarily.
choices.classificationReason: It is affordable but restrictive.

choices.label: Essentials underfunded
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: A required category is below its minimum.
choices.laterConsequence: Missed obligations would follow.
choices.immediateFeedback: Cover essential minimums before confirming.
choices.classificationReason: The plan cannot reliably cover needs.

choices.label: Budget above Rs. 100,000
choices.laterConsequence: Debt or missed payments would otherwise appear.
choices.immediateFeedback: Reduce flexible categories.
choices.classificationReason: The plan uses more than the salary.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Cover every essential minimum, save something, and leave affordable room for enjoyment or flexibility.
reasonableAlternatives: A no-entertainment month may be reasonable temporarily.
Investing may stay at zero while emergency savings are built.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: More saving improves protection; reasonable enjoyment may improve sustainability.

stages.title: Build Emergency Savings
stages.situation: Two months pass. Choose how much of the monthly plan should build emergency savings before the first surprise.
stages.objective: Choose an emergency-saving approach that remains affordable.

startingNode.question: How will you build emergency savings?

choices.label: Save nothing
choices.laterConsequence: The repair may require savings or debt.
choices.immediateFeedback: Unexpected costs may create pressure.
choices.classificationReason: Protection is not built.

choices.label: Save Rs. 5,000 monthly
choices.laterConsequence: Less borrowing may be needed.
choices.immediateFeedback: The amount is manageable but incomplete.
choices.classificationReason: Protection grows gradually.

choices.label: Save Rs. 25,000 monthly
choices.laterConsequence: The plan may become restrictive or invalid.
choices.immediateFeedback: Fast saving helps only when the full budget still works.
choices.classificationReason: The amount may be too large.

choices.label: Save a realistic Rs. 10,000 monthly
choices.laterConsequence: The remainder can use flexible savings.
choices.immediateFeedback: Meaningful protection grows without breaking the example budget.
choices.classificationReason: The target balances protection and affordability.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Build emergency savings consistently without making the monthly budget impossible to maintain.
reasonableAlternatives: A smaller amount fits higher essential costs.
A larger amount fits only when the full plan remains affordable.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: More protection leaves less money for wants and other goals.

stages.title: Handle a Surprise Expense
stages.situation: An essential appliance breaks. The repair costs Rs. 40,000. Earlier emergency, savings, wants, and debt choices determine the available responses.
stages.objective: Predict the intended resource and choose a complete repair plan.

prediction.question: Which resource was designed for this kind of expense?
prediction.explanation: Emergency savings protect the normal budget from genuine surprises.

startingNode.question: How will you fund the repair?

educationalAssumptions: Borrowing Rs. 40,000 creates ten equal classroom repayments of Rs. 4,000.
No interest or lender fee is invented.

choices.label: Use the emergency fund
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Up to Rs. 40,000 is deducted from emergency savings.
choices.shortTermConsequence: The repair is completed without debt.
choices.laterConsequence: Emergency savings need rebuilding.
choices.immediateFeedback: The fund performs its intended purpose.
choices.classificationReason: Enough emergency money must exist.

choices.label: Use general savings
choices.laterConsequence: Goal progress becomes harder.
choices.immediateFeedback: The repair is covered, but another priority slows.
choices.classificationReason: Accessible savings can solve the problem.

choices.label: Borrow the full amount
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Debt rises by Rs. 40,000 and monthly repayment becomes Rs. 4,000.
choices.laterConsequence: Future goal and investment capacity fall.
choices.immediateFeedback: Borrowing may be necessary when savings are insufficient.
choices.classificationReason: Repayment creates future pressure.

choices.label: Skip an essential payment
choices.laterConsequence: Investment readiness decreases.
choices.immediateFeedback: This moves the problem rather than solving it.
choices.classificationReason: An essential obligation remains uncovered.

choices.label: Combine savings and reduced wants
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Emergency savings, optional spending, then general savings fund Rs. 40,000.
choices.shortTermConsequence: The repair is completed without new debt.
choices.laterConsequence: Savings fall and enjoyment is reduced.
choices.immediateFeedback: This works when the emergency fund is still small.
choices.classificationReason: Several flexible sources share the cost.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Use sufficient emergency savings; otherwise combine accessible savings and flexible spending before avoidable debt.
reasonableAlternatives: General savings may be used when emergency savings are small.
Borrowing may be necessary when accessible resources are insufficient.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: Savings reduce future protection; debt preserves cash but creates repayment pressure.

stages.title: Avoid a Financial Scam
stages.situation: A message guarantees that Rs. 25,000 will become Rs. 50,000 next week and demands secrecy.
stages.objective: Identify warning signs and choose a safe or risky response.

config.message: Invest Rs. 25,000 today and receive Rs. 50,000 next week. Returns are guaranteed. Keep this private.

sortableItems.label: Send money to a personal account

config.ambiguityExplanation: Referral rewards are not proof of fraud or safety.

choices.label: Send Rs. 25,000 immediately
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Rs. 25,000 is lost in the fictional scam.
choices.laterConsequence: Goal and emergency capacity weaken.
choices.immediateFeedback: Professional design did not prove safety.
choices.classificationReason: Guarantees, urgency, and secrecy were accepted.

choices.label: Ask for more testimonials
choices.laterConsequence: Independent verification is still needed.
choices.immediateFeedback: Testimonials may be selected or false.
choices.classificationReason: The promoter controls the evidence.

choices.label: Verify independently
choices.laterConsequence: Later goals are unaffected by scam loss.
choices.immediateFeedback: Independent checks are stronger than appearance.
choices.classificationReason: Information is checked outside the promoter’s control.

choices.label: Refuse to act under pressure
choices.laterConsequence: The offer may be checked later or ignored.
choices.immediateFeedback: A genuine opportunity should allow time for review.
choices.classificationReason: Urgency is rejected.

choices.label: Share banking passwords
choices.laterConsequence: The learner must choose another response.
choices.immediateFeedback: Never share passwords or security codes.
choices.classificationReason: Sensitive credentials cannot be used for verification.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Refuse pressure and verify the company, payment destination, risks, and claims independently.
reasonableAlternatives: Ignoring the message is reasonable when the learner does not wish to investigate.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: Verification takes time but protects savings and control.

stages.title: Set and Fund a Long-Term Goal
stages.situation: Build a Rs. 180,000 laptop or education goal. Debt repayments, scam losses, emergency savings, and the monthly budget now determine what is realistic.
stages.objective: Create a measurable goal that fits the current state.

choices.label: Create an affordable measurable plan
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: The selected monthly contribution starts in Month 7.
choices.laterConsequence: Investing capacity falls by the goal contribution.
choices.immediateFeedback: The goal becomes measurable and connected to the budget.
choices.classificationReason: Amount, deadline, contribution, and priority fit.

choices.label: Extend the deadline
choices.laterConsequence: The goal may finish after the simulated year.
choices.immediateFeedback: A delayed realistic goal is stronger than an unaffordable deadline.
choices.classificationReason: Time is traded for affordability.

choices.label: Borrow the missing goal amount
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Debt rises by the goal gap.
choices.laterConsequence: Investment readiness decreases.
choices.immediateFeedback: Borrowing may accelerate the goal but creates repayment pressure.
choices.classificationReason: The deadline is forced with debt.

choices.label: Remove emergency savings for the goal
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Emergency savings move into goal progress.
choices.laterConsequence: Future surprises become harder.
choices.immediateFeedback: The goal advances by weakening protection.
choices.classificationReason: A long-term goal replaces emergency readiness.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Set an amount, deadline, contribution, and priority that fit debt, emergency needs, and the real budget.
reasonableAlternatives: Extend the deadline when the original contribution is unaffordable.
Reduce the amount when the goal itself can change.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: A faster goal uses more monthly capacity; a longer deadline preserves flexibility.

stages.title: Decide Whether to Invest
stages.situation: Consider a regular monthly investment. Essentials, emergency savings, debt, goal contributions, and available cash determine whether it fits.
stages.objective: Complete the readiness check and choose an affordable investment or delay plan.

readinessChecks: money can stay invested for years
allocationRules: diversification reduces concentration risk, not all risk
educationalAssumptions: Three monthly contributions occur before the decline.
No fees, taxes, or guaranteed returns are included.
config.requiredDisclaimer: These values are fictional. Investments may rise or fall, and no recovery or profit is guaranteed.

choices.label: Invest all available savings
choices.laterConsequence: A decline may force a sale for short-term needs.
choices.immediateFeedback: A larger investment balance does not prove stronger health.
choices.classificationReason: Too much accessible money is exposed.

choices.label: Invest next month’s bill money
choices.laterConsequence: The learner must choose another plan.
choices.immediateFeedback: Money needed soon should remain accessible.
choices.classificationReason: The time horizon does not fit.

choices.label: Begin an affordable diversified contribution
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Three monthly contributions enter fictional diversified assets.
choices.laterConsequence: The balance faces the Stage 7 decline.
choices.immediateFeedback: Regular investing reduces dependence on one entry point without guaranteeing profit.
choices.classificationReason: The foundation and contribution fit.

choices.label: Avoid investing forever
choices.laterConsequence: Future opportunities are rejected without review.
choices.immediateFeedback: Investing is optional, but suitability can change.
choices.classificationReason: Permanent refusal may ignore future goals.

choices.label: Delay while rebuilding emergency savings
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: No investment begins and spare capacity supports the emergency fund.
choices.laterConsequence: Investing may begin later.
choices.immediateFeedback: Delaying may be stronger than investing before readiness.
choices.classificationReason: Foundation comes before market exposure.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Invest affordably only after needs, emergency protection, debt, and near-term goals are covered.
reasonableAlternatives: Delay when emergency savings or debt management remains weak.
Stay in cash for near-term goals.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: Investing offers uncertain growth; cash offers access and lower short-term uncertainty.

stages.title: Respond to a Market Decline
stages.situation: Any investment created in Month 9 falls 15%. Explore three possible paths and decide how to respond without assuming recovery or permanent failure.
stages.objective: Respond to uncertainty using the complete financial state.

timeline.contributionsRule: Continued affordable contributions are added after monthly simulated movement.

investmentSimulator.requiredDisclaimer: These paths are fictional and are not forecasts. Markets may recover, remain weak, or fall further.

choices.label: Sell everything immediately
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: The portfolio moves to cash and the current result becomes realised.
choices.laterConsequence: Later movement does not affect the sold amount.
choices.immediateFeedback: Selling removes uncertainty but may be emotion-led.
choices.classificationReason: The choice is based only on the fall.

choices.label: Review the goal and investment quality
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: No automatic sale or purchase occurs.
choices.shortTermConsequence: The portfolio remains exposed during review.
choices.laterConsequence: The learner may continue, pause, reduce, or sell after evidence.
choices.immediateFeedback: Review prevents fear or hope from being the only reason.
choices.classificationReason: Time horizon, fees, diversification, and quality are checked.

choices.label: Continue the affordable contribution
choices.laterConsequence: The final value depends on the fictional path.
choices.immediateFeedback: Regular contributions do not guarantee recovery.
choices.classificationReason: The amount still fits after review.

choices.label: Borrow to recover the loss
choices.immediateFinancialEffect: Debt and investment exposure each rise by Rs. 50,000.
choices.laterConsequence: Debt pressure remains regardless of market result.
choices.immediateFeedback: Borrowing does not reverse the existing decline.
choices.classificationReason: Certain repayment is added to uncertain performance.

choices.label: Invest emergency savings
choices.laterConsequence: A later emergency may require debt or sale.
choices.immediateFeedback: Lower prices do not guarantee profit.
choices.classificationReason: Protection is exchanged for uncertainty.

choices.label: Ignore everything
choices.laterConsequence: Genuine problems may be missed.
choices.immediateFeedback: Avoiding panic does not replace review.
choices.classificationReason: Long-term investing still needs monitoring.

recommendedDecisionLogic.strongestApproach: Review the goal, quality, diversification, and affordability before a major change.
reasonableAlternatives: Sell when the investment no longer fits the goal or quality requirements.
recommendedDecisionLogic.tradeOff: Staying invested keeps uncertainty; selling realises the current result and ends exposure.

debrief.title: The Year Was Built One Decision at a Time
debrief.content: You managed salary, needs, enjoyment, savings, an emergency, debt, a scam, a measurable goal, investment readiness, and a market decline. No single choice created the result. Early budgeting changed emergency options. Debt and scam losses changed goal capacity. Emergency protection and the goal changed whether investing was suitable. The final investment balance mattered, but it did not replace needs coverage, debt control, scam awareness, or accessible savings. One weak choice also did not end the year; later adjustments could improve the plan. Financial strength came from repeated, connected, and realistic decisions—not one lucky investment.
debrief.simpleSummary: Strong finances come from connected decisions repeated and adjusted over time.

realLifeChallenge.title: Write Your Five-Part Plan
realLifeChallenge.instruction: Create a fictional monthly plan with five headings: needs, wants, emergency savings, one goal, and long-term money. Use no real account details and make no transaction.
